summary: Two range lights marking the south entrance to Baynes Sound, off Denman Island, B.C.: first lit 1891, staffed by the Coast Guard, reached by boat only.

structures.note: Red daymark with white stripe (CCG list)
Round fibreglass tower with lantern replaced the 1922 steel tower and the skeletal tower (LF)

access.note: Staffed Coast Guard lightstation: the keepers' home and workplace. Visit only where the station welcomes visitors, and never land uninvited. Lighthouse Friends says the grounds are open and the tower closed; the Lighthouse Directory, as quoted in the record, says closed to visitors.

visit.note: Best seen from the overlook at Boyle Point Provincial Park (LF)

events.note: First lit New Year's Day 1891 by keeper Tom H. Piercy
Lantern and illuminating apparatus sent to Egg Island; upper tower taken down, lower part roofed as a dwelling
Two range lights commenced operation 16 July 1898
Steamer Alpha stranded on Yellow Island in a gale and fog, total loss
Fog-alarm building completed and 1 1/2-inch diaphone installed (report year ended 31 March 1908)
Steel tower with revolving light, flashing every six seconds, begun March 1922
New dwelling built after the keeper's complaint
Renamed Chrome Island around 1940 (Lighthouse Friends); CoastView gives 1923 for the change from Yellow Island
Anchor of the Alpha recovered and placed on a cement block near the Denman ferry landing
Skeletal tower brought down and replaced by round fibreglass tower
Archaeological study; island now a protected archaeological site (petroglyphs, shell midden)
Keeper Roger Williamson helped a couple whose boat was swamped near the island

corrections.why: Lighthouse Friends says the 1891 tower's lantern was removed and the tower reduced to a dwelling in 1898, and gives a wooden front light of 1898. The build year of the present front tower is not in any source read, so the record's 1891 for the front range light needs a human check; no value is proposed.
No source read gives 7.5 m. The CCG list gives the front light's focal height as 14.0 m; the structure height is not stated.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 'F Y' is the front light; Wikidata's 'Fl W 5s' matches the rear light, which the CCG list gives as Fl W Y 5s (a white light flashing every five seconds, with a yellow light visible in line of the range).
The 14.0 m figure is the front light (CCG). The 22 m figure in Wikidata matches the rear light, whose focal height the CCG list gives as 21.9 m.
The Department's reports call it Yellow Island and Lighthouse Friends says the Chrome name came about 1940; CoastView says 1923. The sources disagree and the story says so.

Department's list gives nine (master and eight crew, including three engineers); the wire report of 19 December 1900 names eight dead, including two engineers; Lighthouse Friends gives seven (the owner, captain and five others clinging to the mainmast).

notes_for_editor: Keeper names and years for 1891-1922 come from Lighthouse Friends' head-keeper list. John Doney (1906 list, scan 185, printed 176) was matched by column position in the OCR; the 1912 list (scan 81 of the 1913 volume) also reads 'Yellow island J- Doney'. The page images could not be opened from the review session (the archive.org image host refused the connection), so every column match was checked against the OCR text only, with the second table as corroboration. Identity of 'Yellow island': the 1901 casualty list says 'Yellow Island, Baynes Sound, B.C.' and the 1908 entry (rectangular wooden building, li-inch diaphone) matches Lighthouse Friends' 1908 diaphone account, but Lighthouse Friends also mentions a Yellow Island in Discovery Passage, so the 1907 and 1908 entries are identified by content, not by name: worth a human look. Death toll: Department 9; wire report names eight (two engineers); Lighthouse Friends seven. The 1891 first-lighting date rests on Lighthouse Friends and CoastView; the 1891 Department report is not in the local corpus. The record's 'grounds closed' conflicts with Lighthouse Friends' 'grounds open'; the story gives Lighthouse Friends' version. The 1½-inch figure is not used because the report's OCR reads 'li-inch'. Post-1960 keepers and the 2009 rescue are named only as Lighthouse Friends prints them. Wikipedia not used.
